entries.title: Persuasion: Who Knows Where to Find Help?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: In Persuasion, an accident leaves the group frightened. Anne asks for a surgeon. Captain Wentworth starts to go, but Anne suggests Captain Benwick instead.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Why change the messenger? Benwick knows where a surgeon can be found. Anne chooses local knowledge, not simply the first person ready to run.

entries.prompt: Who knows where to find the surgeon: Wentworth or Benwick?
entries.answer: Benwick. Anne chooses the person who knows the way.
entries.visualBrief: Bright refined anime illustration of adult Regency Anne calmly directing an adult gentleman along a coastal town street, urgent but non-graphic, no injured person visible, hands out of frame, quiet center for captions, no text.

entries.title: Game-Day English: Rooting or Winning?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The team in blue. But they're two points behind.

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: So you support blue, even though blue isn't winning?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Exactly. Rooting for a team means supporting it. If you want the score, ask: Who's ahead?

entries.prompt: Which question asks about support: Who are you rooting for, or who's ahead?
entries.answer: Who are you rooting for? Who's ahead asks which team is winning.
entries.visualBrief: Bright high quality anime illustration of auburn-haired adult woman in teal cardigan and dark-blond adult man in blue-gray hoodie enjoying a home watch party, generic field on small TV, no real logos or scores, faces in outer upper thirds, quiet center for captions, no text.

entries.title: Persuasion: A Friend Who Stayed
entries.hook: The support was not a speech.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Captain Harville tells Anne how Wentworth helped their grieving friend Benwick. Wentworth travelled night and day to reach Portsmouth.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Then he stayed with Benwick for a week. The important detail is not a clever thing he said. It is the time he gave. Listen for the action that shows friendship.

entries.prompt: Did Wentworth send a letter and leave, or travel there and stay?
entries.answer: He travelled there and stayed for a week. The action shows his care.
entries.visualBrief: Bright warm anime-adjacent Regency illustration of two adult gentlemen in a quiet harbor lodging, one sitting beside the other with a reassuring expression, thoughtful friendship, no injury or tragedy imagery, hands below frame, quiet center for captions, no lettering.

entries.title: Watch-Party English: When Should You Ask?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I don't understand that play. Everyone is watching so closely. Should I ask now?

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: Wait until a break. Then ask: What happened there? You don't need to pretend you know every rule.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: What happened there? That's one simple question, at a better time.

entries.prompt: When is it easier to ask: during a tense play, or at a break?
entries.answer: At a break. Ask what happened there, without interrupting the moment.
entries.visualBrief: Bright colorful anime illustration of an adult blue-gray hoodied male beginner and auburn-haired teal-cardigan female friend chatting at a snack table during a watch-party break, television softly blurred, warm lively palette, quiet center, hands out of frame, no text or logos.
